reports.title: Charles River Laboratories Announces Third-Quarter 2026 Results

guidance.heading: 2026 Guidance Update
section: The Company is increasing its 2026 revenue and earnings per share guidance, which was last updated on August 5, 2026. This increase primarily reflects the third-quarter outperformance, which was principally driven by the better-than-expected performance in the DSA segment and a lower tax rate. On a GAAP basis, the Company is also increasing its earnings per share guidance, due primarily to the third-quarter benefit associated with the reversal of acquired tax reserves.
The Company’s 2026 guidance for revenue and earnings per share is as follows:

2026 GUIDANCE | CURRENT | PRIOR
Revenue growth/(decrease), reported | (2.0)% - (1.5)% | (3.5)% - (2.5)%
Less: Contribution from acquisitions | 0.0% - (0.5)% | 0.0% - (0.5)%
Add: Impact from divestitures | ~4.5% | ~4.5%
Less: Favorable impact of foreign exchange | (0.5)% - (1.0)% | (0.5)% - (1.0)%
Revenue growth/(decrease), organic (1) | At least +1.5% | 0.0% - 1.0%
GAAP EPS estimate | $8.15 – $8.35 | $3.05 – $3.35
Acquisition-related amortization (2) | ~$2.10 | ~$2.30
Acquisition- and divestiture-related costs (3) | ~$4.70 | ~$4.75
Reversal of acquired tax reserves (4) | ($5.03) | --
Costs associated with restructuring and efficiency initiatives (5) | ~$1.50 | ~$1.20
Other, net (6) | ($0.03) | ($0.17)
Non-GAAP EPS estimate | $11.35 – $11.55 | $11.15 – $11.45

desk.headline: Adjusted EPS up 27% to $3.09, beat; organic sales up 4.7%; 2026 revenue and EPS outlook raised
results: Revenue fell 2.2% to $982.7m after businesses were sold in May, but grew 4.7% like-for-like, the second quarter of growth in a row.
Adjusted EPS rose 27% to $3.09 on wider margins and a lower tax rate; GAAP EPS of $6.86 includes a one-off $5.06 tax reserve release.
Drug safety testing (DSA) grew 5.9% organically on more regulated studies; research models (RMS) fell 0.6%.
The company has spent $324m on share buybacks so far this year.

guidance.summary: Charles River raised its 2026 outlook: organic growth of at least 1.5% and adjusted EPS of $11.35–11.55. The higher GAAP EPS range mainly reflects the one-off tax benefit.

points: Management described drugmaker demand as strong, with more proposals from biotech and pharma clients.
Safety assessment bookings ran ahead of revenue, with a book-to-bill above 1x.
Discounting is easing, but price gains are not expected to show until the second half of 2027.
Lower costs for large research models helped margins.
The Create the Future programme targets more than $300m of savings over four years.
call.source: Press release (Exhibit 99.1); StockStory, 5 Nov 2026; BioSpectrum Asia, 5 Nov 2026

watch: Whether safety assessment bookings keep running ahead of revenue.
When price increases start to show up in revenue.
Progress on the cost-savings programme and the weaker research models unit.
